3-5.title: The Class Pet
3-5.prompt: Your class can get a fish or a hamster. Which pet should the class get? Explain why.
3-5.promptEs: Tu clase puede tener un pez o un hámster. ¿Qué mascota debe tener la clase? Explica por qué.

responses.text: The class should get a hamster. Hamsters are fun and you can hold them and they are soft.
I like fish. Fish is good.

I think our class should get a fish. First, a fish is easy to care for because we only need to feed it once a day. Also, a fish stays in its tank, so it cannot escape when we are at lunch. Although a hamster is soft, it sleeps all day and is awake at night when nobody is here.

3-5.title: A Butterfly Grows
3-5.prompt: Describe the life cycle of a butterfly. Tell the stages in order.
3-5.promptEs: Describe el ciclo de vida de una mariposa. Cuenta las etapas en orden.

responses.text: A butterfly goes through four stages. First, it begins as a tiny egg on a leaf. Next, a caterpillar hatches and eats leaves so that it can grow bigger. Then the caterpillar forms a hard case called a chrysalis, where its body changes. Finally, an adult butterfly comes out, and it lays eggs to start the cycle again.
The butterfly is a egg and then it is a butterfly.
First the butterfly is a egg. Then it is a caterpillar and it eats a lot. Then it is in a cocoon and then it is a butterfly.

features.text: It has the most sentences.
features.why: More sentences do not help unless each one adds a clear idea.

features.text: It tells all four stages in order with First, Next, Then, and Finally.
features.why: Order words help the reader follow each stage.

features.text: It uses so that and where to explain why and where things happen.
features.why: These words add a reason or a place inside one sentence.

features.text: It uses science words like hatches and chrysalis.
features.why: Science words tell exactly what happens.

features.text: It uses the biggest words it can find.
features.why: Big words help only when they fit the idea and are used correctly.

3-5.title: Our Museum Trip
3-5.prompt: Tell about a class trip to a museum or a special place in your town. What happened first, next, and last?
3-5.promptEs: Cuenta sobre una excursión de tu clase a un museo o a un lugar especial de tu ciudad. ¿Qué pasó primero, después y al final?

responses.text: We went to the museum. We saw old things and we ate lunch and we went home on the bus.

Last spring, my class visited the history museum downtown. When we arrived, a guide showed us tools that farmers used two hundred years ago. Next, we tried grinding corn with a heavy stone, which was harder than it looked. After lunch, we drew pictures of old houses. On the bus ride home, I told my friend that grinding corn was my favorite part.
The trip was fun. We see a lot of stuff.

3-5.title: Bags of Apples
3-5.prompt: Maya has 4 bags with 6 apples in each bag. How many apples does she have? Explain how you solved the problem.
3-5.promptEs: Maya tiene 4 bolsas con 6 manzanas en cada bolsa. ¿Cuántas manzanas tiene? Explica cómo resolviste el problema.

responses.text: She has 24 apples. I count.
Maya has 24 apples. I did 6 plus 6 plus 6 plus 6 and I got 24.

Maya has 24 apples. There are 4 equal groups with 6 apples in each group, so I multiplied 4 times 6. To check my answer, I added 6 four times, and I got 24 again. Because both ways match, I know my answer is correct.

features.text: It writes the answer at the very start.
features.why: Giving the answer is good, but explaining how you got it is what makes it strong.

features.text: It gives the answer, explains the steps, and then checks the answer.
features.why: A full explanation shows every part of your thinking.

features.text: It uses so and because to show why each step makes sense.
features.why: So and because connect each step to its reason.

features.text: It uses math words like equal groups, multiplied, and check.
features.why: Math words tell exactly what you did.

features.text: It uses the number 6 many times.
features.why: Repeating numbers does not explain your thinking.

6-8.title: Ban Plastic Bags?
6-8.prompt: Some towns have stopped stores from giving out plastic bags. Should your town do the same? Use what you know about plastic and the environment.
6-8.promptEs: Algunas ciudades no permiten que las tiendas den bolsas de plástico. ¿Debería tu ciudad hacer lo mismo? Usa lo que sabes sobre el plástico y el medio ambiente.

responses.text: Yes, my town should stop plastic bags. Plastic is bad for the ocean and animals eat it and they get sick. People can use other bags.

I believe our town should stop stores from giving out plastic bags. First, plastic bags do not break down for hundreds of years, so they pile up in landfills and rivers. In addition, sea turtles often mistake floating bags for jellyfish, which can block their stomachs. Some people argue that plastic bags are convenient, but reusable cloth bags are just as easy to carry. As a result, a ban would protect wildlife without making shopping harder.
Plastic bags are bad. The town should do the same.

features.text: It gives two reasons, answers the other side, and ends with a conclusion.
features.why: A strong argument builds reasons and answers people who disagree.

features.text: It starts with I believe.
features.why: Starting with I believe is fine, but the reasons and evidence make it strong.

features.text: It uses complex sentences with so, which, and but to link ideas.
features.why: These words show cause, add detail, and compare ideas.

features.text: It uses precise words like landfills, wildlife, and break down.
features.why: Precise words make the evidence clear and believable.

features.text: It uses the most words.
features.why: Length alone does not make an answer strong; ideas and connections do.

6-8.title: Solving It Together
6-8.prompt: Tell about a time you had to solve a problem with a partner or a team. What happened, and how did it end?
6-8.promptEs: Cuenta sobre una vez que tuviste que resolver un problema con un compañero o un equipo. ¿Qué pasó y cómo terminó?

responses.text: In sixth grade, my partner and I had to build a bridge out of paper for science class. At first, our bridge collapsed as soon as we placed one coin on it. Instead of giving up, we studied a picture of a real bridge and noticed the triangles in its design. We folded the paper into triangles, which made it much stronger. When the teacher tested it, our bridge held twenty coins. I learned that a mistake can show you what to try next.
We had a problem and we fix it. It was hard.
My team made a poster and we did not agree. Then we talked and we picked the colors and it looked good. We got a good grade.

6-8.prompt: A store sells 3 notebooks for 6 dollars. How much would 7 notebooks cost? Explain how you solved it.
6-8.promptEs: Una tienda vende 3 cuadernos por 6 dólares. ¿Cuánto costarían 7 cuadernos? Explica cómo lo resolviste.

responses.text: It costs 14 dollars. I found one notebook is 2 dollars and I did 2 times 7.
14. I did times.

Seven notebooks would cost 14 dollars. First, I found the unit rate by dividing 6 dollars by 3 notebooks, which gave me 2 dollars per notebook. Then I multiplied 2 dollars by 7 notebooks to get 14 dollars. To check, I made a ratio table that went from 3 notebooks for 6 dollars to 6 notebooks for 12 dollars, so 7 notebooks for 14 dollars made sense.

6-8.title: Gift of the Nile
6-8.prompt: Explain why the Nile River was important to people in ancient Egypt.
6-8.promptEs: Explica por qué el río Nilo era importante para las personas del antiguo Egipto.

responses.text: The Nile was important. It had water for the people.

The Nile River was the center of life in ancient Egypt for several reasons. Every summer, the river flooded and left behind rich, dark soil, which allowed farmers to grow wheat and barley in the desert. Because the land around it was so dry, the Nile was also the main source of drinking water. In addition, Egyptians used boats on the river to trade goods and carry heavy stones for building. As a result, most cities and farms were built along its banks.
The Nile was important because people need water. They use it for farm and drink. Also they go on boats.

features.text: It explains three ways people used the Nile and ends with a result.
features.why: Several developed reasons and a conclusion make the explanation complete.

features.text: It uses the words ancient Egypt, just like the question.
features.why: Using words from the question is fine, but new reasons and details make it strong.

features.text: It uses complex sentences with which and because to explain causes.
features.why: These words show how one fact causes another.

features.text: It uses precise words like flooded, soil, trade, and banks.
features.why: Precise words give the reader exact information.

features.text: It sounds like a textbook.
features.why: Sounding formal is not enough; clear reasons and connections are what count.

upgrade.model: The Nile was important because it flooded each year and left rich soil for farming.
